subject: Close window: stabilization intervention & MAP rebaseline request
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@heliumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Helium Health Procurement <procurement@heliumhealth.com>, James Liu <james.liu@heliumhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close window: stabilization ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the partnership so far — we wanted to flag a risk that will likely push our go-live. Our security/compliance team just kicked off a last-minute SOC2 scoping review focused on data zoning and that has introduced a 3-week hold on procurement sign-off. Separately, our legal team needs a clarifying clause around data retention that we didn't anticipate.

We understand this is late in the process and want to avoid derailing the project, so two quick asks: can Redwood create a short MAP addendum to rebaseline the acceptance milestones (targeting a new go-live of ~2026-09-15) and can we discuss a temporary credit or goodwill concession to offset the impact to our internal program?

I've attached the procurement questionnaire and the compliance note the SOC2 team sent. Can we lock a 30-minute sync tomorrow to run through the MAP addendum language and credit options?

Appreciate your help — Sarah

Attachments referenced: procurement_questionnaire.pdf (pdf), compliance_scope.docx (docx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Close window: stabilization ask

Sarah — thanks for the heads up and for the context. Sorry to hear about the SOC2 scope hit; we see that pattern occasionally and have a short intervention playbook for it.

Proposed immediate steps (high level):
1) MAP addendum: we can draft an addendum today to rebaseline acceptance to 2026-09-15 and convert the current milestones into a 3-week contingency ladder. I'll attach a draft MAP_v2.xlsx for working edits.
2) Interim access: provide sandbox + read-only telemetry to your compliance reviewers so they can validate flows without requiring production data.
3) Goodwill credit: we can propose a one-time credit (we typically structure this as either a percentage off first invoice or a fixed discount). I'll need internal approval for anything over $15k.
4) Weekly check-ins: short 30-minute status calls (Wednesdays) until go-live to keep blockers visible.

Aditya/Priyom — can you review the attached draft MAP and the compliance notes Sarah referenced? Please push a short risk appendix back to me (risk items + mitigations) and indicate whether we can commit to sandbox telemetry by EOD. Also flag whether a one-time credit up to $18k is approvable or if I need an exec sign-off.

Sarah — if this approach sounds ok, I'll send the draft addendum + risk appendix and book the sync for tomorrow (09:30 PT).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Marissa — quick internal read. Quoting your note below for context:

On 2026-08-09 at 11:05, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Proposed immediate steps (high level):
> 1) MAP addendum: we can draft an addendum today...

Feasibility notes from infra/ops:
- Sandbox telemetry: feasible. We can spin up a time-limited read-only workspace and provide telemetry snapshots redacted for PII. ETA: 48 hours to provision with compliance-friendly filters.
- Capacity: current Dedicated slot can absorb the go-live without additional GPU commit if we accept a soft throughput cap for the first two weeks (we'll enable aggressive caching + shorter seq-length defaults). That mitigates risk but we should document impact on stress-test SLAs.
- Risk items (high level):
  * SOC2 scope may require data residency certs — if required, timeline slips > 3 weeks.
  * Legal redline on retention could change contract terms; vendor legal needs to be looped immediately.

I've put detailed points into risk_appendix.pdf (attached) and highlighted the mitigations we can offer. On the credit: we are comfortable recommending up to $18,000 as a one-time concession applied to the first invoice, but anything above that needs Karthik/exec approval.

Karthik — please advise on approval threshold for credits over $18k; if you confirm, I'll draft the credit term language for legal.

—Aditya

Date: 2026-08-11T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: Helium Health — approval request for goodwill credit & MAP addendum

Karthik — escalating for a quick decision. Thread summary below and requested approvals.

Summary: Helium Health's SOC2 scoping and a late legal retention ask have created a ~3-week procurement hold that will push acceptance beyond our contract's original go-live window. Customer has requested (1) a MAP addendum to rebaseline to 2026-09-15 and (2) a conversation about a goodwill concession.

What we've done: drafted MAP addendum (MAP_v2.xlsx), provision offer for sandbox telemetry (48h), and produced a risk appendix outlining mitigation steps and potential failure modes (risk_appendix.pdf). Aditya recommends a one-time credit up to $18,000 applied to the first invoice; >$18k requires exec sign-off.

Request: please authorize one of the following by EOD tomorrow so I can finalize terms with the customer and route to legal for a quick addendum:
A) Approve one-time credit up to $18,000 (no further approvals needed).
B) Approve up to $25,000 (exec sign-off granted; legal will still finalize language).
C) Decline credit but approve MAP addendum and operational mitigations, and authorize CS to escalate retention FAQ materials to the customer.

Recommendation: I recommend option A to preserve margin but keep the account on track. The customer's program lead (James Liu) signaled that a modest concession will keep the timeline and budget intact; the alternative is a multi-week procurement restart risk.

If you approve A, I'll attach proposed_credit_terms.docx and request legal to fast-track the addendum + a 3-week contingency ladder in the MAP. If you prefer B, I'll request an executive note and adjust terms accordingly.

Thanks for the quick read — I can hop on a 15-min call if helpful.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
